doc: BD field map of ONE 49 Financial client Performance Report (FWD-9), sliced on its Run Report bases. Field NAMES and STRUCTURE only; no client value, name, account number, date, holding or amount. Opal sources are read from code; Black Diamond sources are named from the estate's pull code or from the HAR teardown and every row says which.

input.form: one Black Diamond PDF read in place from outside the repo (never copied)

extractor: data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_custody/bd_field_map.py (extract); the rows add the worker's reads of Opal and BD code
commonwealth_note: FWD-9 asks where Commonwealth's history holds more than Black Diamond's feed. Commonwealth is the Cottonwood predecessor custodian (FWD-4); this is a 49 Financial report whose Opal history is Schwab silver, so no row claims Commonwealth history.

bd_source_basis.pull-code: the endpoint and response field are read by the estate's own code (bd_adapter.py, opal-assets-bd49f-reporting-pull)
bd_source_basis.har-teardown: named in docs/research/bd_dashboard_teardown/BD_DASHBOARD_HAR_TEARDOWN_20260721.md section 3.1 (not pulled by the estate's code)
bd_source_basis.inferred: matched by field name; not confirmed against a response
bd_source_basis.read-from-rendering: a chart series read by a person from the rendered page (the PDF's charts are raster images with no text layer)

opal_status.MAPPED: Opal reads the same figure (caveats in `reason`)
opal_status.MISSING: no Opal source for the same figure; `reason` says why

denominator.derived_rows_note: a chart's series are read from the rendering (charts are raster images), and a table whose rows are a class hierarchy is split into its total row and its class rows, which map differently
